In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
 Laa No.4 of 2019
 Muralidhar Swain .... Appellant
 Mr. M.K. Panda, Advocate
 -versus-
 State of Odisha & ors. .... Respondents
 Mr. B. Panigrahi, Asc

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Coram: Justice Sanjay Kumar Mishra
 Order
14.05.2024 I.A. No.2 of 2020 Order No.
07 . This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

2. This Application has been filed seeking leave of this Court to prefer the Appeal on the ground that the sole L.R. of the Claimant/Petitioner before the Court below has died living behind present Appellant as his legal heir.

The said claimant died during the pendency of the proceeding before the Court below on 18.01.2015, whereas the impugned order/judgment was passed in L.A.A. Case No.53 of 2006 on 21.03.2018 against a dead person, even though it was brought to the notice of the Court below regarding death of the claimant/Petitioner.
3. In view of the reasons assigned in the application so also submission made by the learned Counsel for the Appellant/Petitioner, prayer for leave to Appeal is allowed.
4. Accordingly, the I.A. stands disposed of.

(S. K. Mishra) Judge Order No.
08. 1.
Heard Mr. Panda, learned Counsel for the Appellant so also Mr. B. Panigrahi, learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State/Respondents.
2. As pointed out by the Stamp Reporter, there is a delay of 258 days in presenting the memorandum of appeal.
A stand has been taken in the I.A. that the Petitioner is a poor daily labourer, who is the sole L.R. of the claimant before the Court below, who died on 18.01.2015.
He was not aware regarding pendency of the said case before the Court below, which was ultimately disposed of confirming the order passed by the LAO.

A further ground has been taken to condone the delay that due to his poor financial condition, he could not come to Cuttack and arrange the relevant documents in time, which resulted delay in presenting the Memorandum of Appeal.

sentences.text:
In view of the above stand of the Petitioner/Appellant, the delay, as pointed out by the Office,
stands condoned.
4. Accordingly, the I.A. stands disposed of.

(S. K. Mishra) Judge Order No.
09. 1.

Though the Appeal is on board under the heading "For Orders" for consideration of the application for seeking leave of this Court to prefer this Appeal so also to condone the delay, in view of order of date passed in I.A. No.2 of 2020 so also I.A. No.49 of 2019, on consent of the learned Counsel for the Appellant so also State/Respondents, the matter is taken up for hearing and final disposal.

2. Heard learned Counsel for the parties.
3.
As is revealed from the impugned order, the Petitioner is dead.

It is further found from the impugned order that the said order was passed on 21.03.2018 referring to the judgment of the Apex Court reported in AIR 2000 (SC) 726, thereby confirming the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer, Kendrapara because of non-taking of steps by the Petitioner.

As stated in the memorandum of appeal, the Petitioner before the Court below, who is the father of the present Appellant, died on 18.01.2015 and the Appellant was not aware about the pendency of the said referral case before the Court below for which he could not take steps to be substituted in the said Appeal, as a result of which the same was disposed of confirming the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer,
Kendrapara thereby debarring the Petitioner to pursue the said referral case for enhancement of the compensation amount.

Learned Counsel for the Appellant submits, if the impugned order is not set aside giving opportunity to the present Appellant to pursue the said case on merit, the Appellant will be irreparably prejudiced.

4. In view of such submission made by learned Counsel for the Appellant and grounds taken in the Memorandum of Appeal, the impugned order dated 21.03.2018 passed in L.A. Case No.53 of 2006 (L.A. No.8/1999) pending in the Court of Civil Judge (Senior Division), Kendrapara is hereby set aside.
5. Matter is remitted back to the Court below giving liberty to the present Appellant to move an application for substitution along with an application for condonation of delay within three weeks'
hence.

entities.text: Court of Civil Judge (Senior Division), Kendrapara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
On filing of such applications, the Court below shall condone the delay in terms of provisions enshrined under Section 14 of the Limitation Act, 1963 and thereafter, consider the application for substitution by substituting the present Appellant in L.A. Case No.53 of 2006 as the legal heir of the deceased Bira Kishore Swain and shall proceed further in accordance with law giving opportunity to the parties to lead evidence and shall do well to conclude the said proceeding within a period of six months from the date of communication/production of the certified copy of this order.
6.
With the aforesaid observation the Appeal stands allowed and disposed of.
